# Copilot instructions — management-project

This repository is an Angular 20 application with optional server-side rendering (SSR). Keep guidance brief, concrete and repository-specific.

Key facts (use these to orient changes):
- Framework: Angular 20 (standalone components / bootstrapApplication).
- SSR: project includes `src/main.server.ts` and `angular.json` has `ssr`/`server` configured; server entry may be `dist/management-project/server/server.mjs` for production (`package.json` script `serve:ssr`).
- Entrypoints: client `src/main.ts`, server bootstrap `src/main.server.ts`. App-level configuration lives in `src/app/app.config.ts` and `src/app/app.config.server.ts`.

Architecture & patterns
- Single-app (no libs). Uses standalone components and `bootstrapApplication` instead of NgModules. Examples: `src/main.ts`, `src/main.server.ts` and `src/app/app.ts`.
- Routing: routes are declared in `src/app/app.routes.ts`. Lazy dashboard routes load `features/dashboards/dashboard-layout/dashboard-routing.module.ts`.
- Features folder structure: `src/app/features/<feature>/<component>` (e.g. `features/auth/login` and `features/dashboards/*`). Follow this layout for new features.
- State & services: small services are provided in root (e.g. `src/app/features/auth/auth.service.ts` uses Angular signals for simple auth state). Prefer signals for lightweight state when matching existing patterns.
- Styles: global `src/styles.scss`, component styles use SCSS (Angular CLI configured default). Add styles to component SCSS files.

Developer workflows & commands
- Local dev (client only): `npm run start:dev` (maps to `ng serve --configuration development`) — open http://localhost:4200.
- Production build + SSR: `npm run build:ssr` then `npm run serve:ssr` runs `node dist/management-project/server/server.mjs`.
- Unit tests: `ng test` via `npm run test` if needed (Karma configured in `angular.json`).

Project-specific conventions
- Use standalone components and `bootstrapApplication` instead of NgModule classes. New components should follow the same bootstrap pattern.
- Route layout: top-level `app.routes.ts` holds route table; dashboard routes are lazy-loaded from `dashboard-routing.module.ts`.
- Public/static assets live in `public/` and are referenced directly in `angular.json` build assets.
- Keep component CSS in the component folder and use SCSS. The project sets Angular schematics default style to `scss` in `angular.json`.

Integration points & external deps
- Express is a runtime dependency for SSR server (`express` in `package.json`). The production server is generated by Angular's SSR build and executed by Node.
- No external API clients are present — `AuthService` contains a stubbed login, so connect real APIs where appropriate and follow the service pattern.

Editing & testing guidance for AI changes
- Small feature: add a component under `src/app/features/<feature>/<name>` with a matching route entry in `src/app/app.routes.ts` or lazy-load via a routing module under `features/<feature>`.
- For SSR-sensitive code, prefer platform checks (e.g. guard window/document access) or use Angular's `isPlatformBrowser` helpers. See `src/main.server.ts` and `src/app/app.config.server.ts` for SSR providers.
- When changing configuration, update `angular.json` and `package.json` scripts if necessary; keep `ssr`/`server` entries intact.

Examples from the codebase
- Auth pattern: `src/app/features/auth/auth.service.ts` — root-provided service using signals and simple API surface: `login(email, password): Promise<boolean>`, `logout()`, `isLoggedIn()`.
- Routing: `src/app/app.routes.ts` shows a combination of direct component routes and lazy loaded modules (`dashboard` lazy loads `dashboard-routing.module`).
- Bootstrapping: `src/main.ts` and `src/main.server.ts` show how `bootstrapApplication` is used with `appConfig` and `config`.
